clue.text: Hearing rumours about son returning

indicators.note: 'about' means going around, so the rumours word wraps the son's letter
something returning goes back the way it came, so the whole combination is read from right to left

blocks.note: 'noises' in the sense of rumblings or talk going round
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone hears gossip about their son coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: NOISES wraps S to make NOISSES, and reading that backwards gives SESSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A court or committee sitting is a session, so a formal hearing is a synonym.

clue.text: One who helps penpal buy elsewhere – only looking in prime locations

indicators.note: prime locations are positions numbered by prime numbers, so only the 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 11th, 13th and 17th letters count

blocks.note: letters 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 and 17 of these three words run together

explanation.surface: Someone trying to help a pen pal shop elsewhere, checking only the best sites.
explanation.walkthrough: Counting along 'penpalbuyelsewhere', the prime-numbered positions hold E, N, A, B, L, E, R. 'Prime locations' reads like property jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: An enabler is a person who makes something possible for another, a helper.

clue.text: Labour start to work in constituency

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
'in' places the kept letter inside the word for a constituency

blocks.note: the opening letter of work
a parliamentary seat is a constituency

explanation.surface: The Labour Party beginning its campaign in a constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' with its capital looks like the political party, but it is the definition: hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat as a noun means hard toil, a synonym for labour.

clue.text: Having continued success performing a part on the radio

indicators.note: what is broadcast on the radio is only heard, so the words go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: an actor who is performing is on stage
a part in a play is a role, which sounds like roll

explanation.surface: An actor keeps getting work, playing a part in a radio drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on a roll is the idiom for enjoying a run of continued success.

clue.text: Long-winded and ever so surprisingly absorbing book

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not what was expected, so these letters come out in a new order
absorbing means taking in, so the rearranged letters soak up the book's letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A reader finds a rambling book is, against expectation, ever so gripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbose means using more words than needed, which is what long-winded describes.

clue.text: Cause to be admired – as 2 drug-hunting Feds replacing expert

indicators.note: replacing means one piece swaps into the spot another occupied in the cross-referenced answer

blocks.note: the answer to 2 down
the Drug Enforcement Administration, the US federal drugs agency
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: The setter, Fed, jokes about being admired like federal drug agents.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ENABLER, remove ABLE and put DEA in its place. The setter's pseudonym Fed adds to the in-joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone loved or liked, so it means cause to be admired.

clue.text: Perhaps rib friend providing fine dishes?

blocks.note: a rib is an example of a bone
Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so china is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone serving a rib to a friend on fancy plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rib' seems to mean tease a friend, but here it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a fine porcelain used for good tableware, so fine dishes are made of it.

clue.text: GP rules out extravagant display

indicators.note: 'out' here means out of place or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A family doctor forbids lavish showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: A splurge is a lavish bout of spending or a showy display.

clue.text: Petulant Express journalist going after moderate

indicators.note: going after sets the order, putting the reporter's letters behind the moderating word

blocks.note: an express train is a quick one
to temper is to moderate or soften
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A cross reporter from the Daily Express newspaper attacks a moderate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going after' puts the journalist after the moderating word. 'Express' looks like the newspaper title but is just fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick-tempered describes someone who loses their temper easily, a near synonym of petulant.

clue.text: Put off stage in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a stage is a phase

explanation.surface: An actor is thrown off the stage during an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' looks theatrical, matching 'stage', but it is used literally as a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To faze someone is to disconcert them, which is to put them off.

clue.text: Really seeing animal's head by grasping under antler, avoiding all medical dramas

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
avoiding all means every instance of the drama abbreviation is left out of the two words
grasping means holding, so the little word wraps around what remains

blocks.note: the first letter of animal
taken as written
taken as written before the deletion
ER is the US hospital drama series

explanation.surface: A wildlife viewer really sees a stag's head beneath its antler while avoiding TV hospital shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Both ERs come out of UNDERANTLER, leaving UNDANTL, which BY grasps; A leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundantly can serve as an intensifier, as in 'abundantly clear', meaning really or very.

clue.text: Drunk left behind outside without money

indicators.note: the word for behind sits outside, wrapping the abbreviation for left
without means lacking, so the money letter is dropped

blocks.note: your behind is your bottom
L is the abbreviation for left
M for money, as in M1/M3 money supply

explanation.surface: A drunk is left behind outside, penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTOM wraps L, then the final M goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Risky holding Republican office?

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the party letter goes within the word for risky

blocks.note: a variant spelling of chancy, meaning risky
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: It is a gamble for a Republican to stand for public office.
explanation.walkthrough: CHANCEY, the less usual spelling of chancy, takes R. The question mark flags that a chancery is just one kind of office.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancery is an office of records or the office of an embassy, an example of an office.

clue.text: Rewriting duet with lyric displaying naivety

indicators.note: rewriting reorders the text, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: duet and lyric taken as written, with 'with' joining them

explanation.surface: A songwriter innocently rewrites a duet's words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' only joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Credulity is a readiness to believe things too easily, which is naivety.

clue.text: Sample recordings poets made somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some unspecified way

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Poets somehow managed to cut some sample recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: Demo tapes are trial recordings made to showcase a band or song, so sample recordings.

clue.text: With record player spinning around this writer has danced

indicators.note: spinning turns something round, so the two letters for a record player are flipped
around means surrounding, so the flipped letters wrap the phrase for the setter

blocks.note: a disc jockey plays records
I've: this writer, the setter, has

explanation.surface: The setter has danced as a turntable spins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record player' is not a turntable but a person who plays records.
explanation.definitionFit: To jive is to dance in a lively swing style, so jived means danced.

clue.text: Fox News ultimately putting pressure on corporation

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept
in an across entry, one thing on another comes after it, so the pressure letter is placed second

blocks.note: the last letter of news
corporation is old slang for a pot belly; tum is the stomach
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Fox News is leaning on a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox News' reads as the US channel, but Fox is the definition, a verb. 'Putting pressure on corporation' sets P after TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump someone is to baffle them, and fox is a British synonym meaning to puzzle.

clue.text: Restaurant getting attention during dispute when upset

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the dispute word reads bottom to top
during means in the middle of, so attention goes inside

blocks.note: to moot is to raise for debate
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A restaurant draws notice during an argument that gets out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea room is a small café serving tea and light meals, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Squad almost came back wasted

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the squad word loses its final letter
back means going backwards, so the joined letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: a detail is a small squad assigned to a duty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A team nearly returned from the match exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: DETAIL minus L is DETAI; with CAME added, the whole reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin from lack of food, as is someone wasted away.

clue.text: Expect ticket – using theatre for play's opening

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter
using one thing for another means it is swapped in in place of it

blocks.note: a coupon is a voucher or ticket
the first letter of play
NT is the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: A theatregoer expects their ticket to get them into a play's opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: The P of COUPON gives way to NT.
explanation.definitionFit: To count on something is to rely on it happening, so to expect it.

clue.text: Show's touring – regularly turf press out

indicators.note: something touring goes all the way around, so the show word encircles the selected letters
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: to exude confidence is to show it
the first and third letters of turf

explanation.surface: A touring show's crew regularly push the stage turf out.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', so 'Show's touring' means the show word goes round the selected letters; 'turf' seems to be stage dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to force or press something out through an opening.

clue.text: Fighting Bill in boxing ring

indicators.note: boxing means putting in a box, so the little word encloses the ring letter

blocks.note: a bill becomes an Act of Parliament when passed
taken as written
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Boxer Bill fighting in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' and 'ring' suggest a prize fight, but boxing just puts IN around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who see action are in combat, so action can mean fighting.

clue.text: Mix for a Hamburger – I will be covered in mush

indicators.note: covered in means enclosed by, so the pronoun goes inside the mush word

blocks.note: paste is a soft mush
ich is German for I, as a native of Hamburg would say it

explanation.surface: A burger in a bun smothered in mushy sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamburger' suggests a burger but means a person from Hamburg, so German.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a medley or imitation made up of borrowed elements, a mix.

clue.text: In court shame is hard to control

blocks.note: someone 'up before the magistrate' is in court
as in 'what a shame', 'what a pity'

explanation.surface: A defendant who is ashamed in court is unruly.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity means self-important and unwilling to accept authority, so hard to control.

clue.text: Parents taking in large island's capital

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing within, so the parents' letters surround the size letter

blocks.note: PA and MA, father and mother
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Parents taking a large holiday house in an island's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Palma is the capital city of the Spanish island of Majorca.

clue.text: You're very good at solving this, for example?

definitions.text: You're very good at solving this, for example?

blocks.clueFragment: You're very good at solving this
blocks.note: surface reading: a solver being told they are skilled at this very crossword
setter's reading: the sentence itself is an example of a piece of praise

explanation.walkthrough: The clue appears to praise the solver, but the whole sentence is one instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone they are very good at something is an expression of praise or admiration.

clue.text: Celebrate youngster embracing university

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the youngster's word wraps the university letter

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A young person celebrates getting into university.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise or extol, a synonym of celebrate in that sense.

clue.text: A character in Greek chorus is hilarious

blocks.note: taken as written
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to chorus is to sing together

explanation.surface: A figure in a Greek tragedy's chorus turns out to be very funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a letter, not a person in a play; the Greek chorus picture is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing means causing laughter, a milder synonym of hilarious.

clue.text: Busy nurse having good time with daughter

blocks.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
G is the abbreviation for good
an age is a period of time
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A busy nurse enjoys some quality time with their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line that is busy is said to be engaged in British usage, and an occupied person is too.
